title: Bioinformatics
tagline: Sequence databases, alignment, BLAST, profiles and hidden Markov models, phylogenetic inference, gene finding, assembly and variant calling, expression analysis and machine learning
summary: Bioinformatics is the computational analysis of biological data, above all of sequences. This course covers the algorithms and statistics behind sequence alignment and database searches, profiles and hidden Markov models, phylogenetic inference, gene finding, genome assembly and variant calling, the analysis of gene expression, and machine learning for biological data.

chapters.title: Biological sequences and databases
chapters.summary: Sequence formats, the major databases and programming for biologists.

chapters.title: Pairwise sequence alignment
chapters.summary: Substitution matrices, gap penalties and the dynamic-programming algorithms of Needleman–Wunsch and Smith–Waterman.

chapters.title: Searching sequence databases
chapters.summary: BLAST and its heuristics, and the statistics of alignment scores and E-values.

chapters.title: Multiple alignment and profiles
chapters.summary: Progressive alignment, sequence profiles and hidden Markov models of protein families.

chapters.title: Phylogenetic inference
chapters.summary: Distance, parsimony, maximum-likelihood and Bayesian methods for building trees from sequences.

chapters.title: Gene finding and annotation
chapters.summary: Hidden Markov models for genes, motif discovery and the annotation of genomes.

chapters.title: Assembly, read mapping and variant calling
chapters.summary: De Bruijn graphs, aligning reads to a reference and calling variants from them.

chapters.title: Analysing gene expression
chapters.summary: Normalisation, differential expression, false discovery rates and the clustering of RNA-sequencing data.

chapters.title: Machine learning in biology
chapters.summary: Classification, dimensionality reduction and deep learning applied to sequences, images and omics data.
